text:
Jacob Fowler stopped all 46 shots he faced on Tuesday in St. Louis, and Montreal beat the Blues 2-0 for its third straight win. Fowler, a 2023 third-round pick who arrived from Boston College after a .940 save percentage there last season, was the first star by a wide margin. Florian Xhekaj, drafted 101st overall in 2023 and up from the Laval Rocket, scored his first NHL goal in the third period on a tip-in, set up by Mike Matheson and Kirby Dach.

The score hides how lopsided the play was. Our deserved-to-win number, the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins, gave STL 72 percent. The Blues out-attempted the Canadiens 80 to 49 and put 46 shots on goal to MTL's 20. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances, had STL at 3.94 and MTL at 3.21. STL owned the third period, out-chancing Montreal 1.96 to 0.62 in expected goals. Fowler's 46 saves were worth 3.94 expected goals against, so he saved about four goals more than an average goalie would have faced those shots.

Montreal did make its own chances count. Zachary Bolduc, a former Blues first-round pick, opened the scoring in the second period on a snap shot that had only a 6 percent chance of going in, and Xhekaj's tip-in carried a 9 percent chance. Alexandre Texier had the best look of the night, a 47 percent chance in the second period that went off target. Matheson logged 23:24 and picked up two assists. Jordan Binnington allowed two on 20 shots for STL, which went 0 for 3 on the power play. The Canadiens leave with three wins in a row, and the Blues will want to know why 46 shots produced nothing.
